name: Ensembl VEP and release-116 plugin data

version.value: Ensembl release 116 (REST); plugin data directories dated 2025-10 to 2026-08

scope: Variant effect prediction tool with offline caches and pre-built data for plugins. The documentation lists 74 plugins in 18 categories (catalogue/evidence/ensembl_vep/plugin_list.json). The release-116 variation directory holds plugin data for Enformer, GENCODE_promoter, LOEUF, MaveDB, PhenotypeOrthologous, ProtVar, RiboSeqORFs, SpliceAI, SpliceVault and mutfunc, besides pangenomes, vcf, gvf and indexed_vep_cache; Ensembl-generated SpliceAI scores for all possible SNVs in MANE Select transcripts (raw and masked, about 27 GB per file with a tabix index, no indels) are under data_files/homo_sapiens/GRCh38/variation_plugins/.
mapping_methods: VEP consequence calling against Ensembl/RefSeq transcripts; plugin files keyed by GRCh38 coordinates.

quantitative.summary: Plugin data carry their source scores (e.g. MaveDB scores, SpliceAI delta scores, LOEUF).

licence.name: Ensembl: no restrictions on data (verified); plugin resources carry upstream terms (e.g. gnomAD notes SpliceAI annotations as CC BY-NC 4.0)
licence.redistribution: Check each plugin resource before redistribution

update_frequency: With each Ensembl release; plugin files updated irregularly (MaveDB file dated 2026-03-09).
coverage_limitations: Plugin data licences are those of the underlying resources. The plugin page states some of them (dbNSFP has separate academic and commercial branches; PromoterAI needs a licence agreement; the AlphaMissense text conflicts with the licence in the data file we hold) and is silent on others
SpliceAI, Enformer, mutfunc, ProtVar and SpliceVault files are large (see the listing evidence); Ensembl does not generate SpliceAI scores for indels
known_omissions: Only the MaveDB plugin file is acquired; the other plugin data are catalogued with their sizes and not fetched
The plugin list was read from the documentation page; the plugins' own code and the data files' internal formats were not inspected

reuse_decision.rationale: Ensembl already integrates MaveDB, LOEUF, SpliceAI, SpliceVault, ProtVar, mutfunc and Enformer for VEP; reuse these rather than re-deriving them. The MaveDB file is acquired first to measure overlap with the API-built set.

status.notes: FTP listings and the plugin documentation page are reachable (the page returned HTTP 504 in an earlier probe and was read on retry). MaveDB CHECKSUMS file lists BSD sum 22727 / 547461 KiB.

unverified_fields: per-plugin data licences not stated on the plugin page

mechanism_evidence.note: rule-based consequence terms (for example frameshift, stop gained) against transcript models

components.name: predictor plugins (for example SpliceAI, SpliceVault, Enformer, AlphaMissense)

evidence_profile.biological_context: A tool that annotates variants against transcript models and attaches plugin data. Every annotation is computed or looked up per transcript, so one variant can carry different consequences across transcripts and tools.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Mixed, and inherited from the plugin: consequence terms are deterministic rules against annotation, predictor plugins are hypotheses, MaveDB values are measurements and LOEUF is a gene-level population estimate. The evidence kind of each part persists.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate depending on the plugin. A consequence term names a molecular consequence class and does not show loss versus gain of function or tissue context; agreement between predictor plugins is not independent confirmation because they can share training data.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A missing plugin value means that plugin has no data for the variant (type, transcript or build); for example precomputed SpliceAI files cover SNVs in MANE Select transcripts and no indels. Absence is not a negative prediction.
